title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Seen Enough September Surges to Know This One's Real
summary: 69.2% accuracy on Sep 26 keeps the model rolling into the final weekend

content.value:
## Another Day, Another 69% Win Rate

You know what I love about late September baseball? The stakes are high, the rotations are scrambled, and yet somehow the patterns still hold. We went 9-4 yesterday with a 69.2% hit rate, and if you've been around this game as long as I have, you know that's exactly the kind of consistency that separates the noise from the signal.

## The Hits and Misses

The Dodgers took care of business against the Giants at 63% confidence—no surprises there when you've got that kind of pitching advantage. The Rays came through at 61% against the Phillies, and the Braves handled the Marlins exactly as expected at 60%.

The misses? Well, the Mets pulled one out in Washington despite us leaning Nationals. The Jays couldn't deliver at home against the Reds, the Guardians outplayed our Royals pick, and the Red Sox stumbled against the Rockies. Four misses, but none of them were high-confidence calls. That's baseball in September—you take your 69% and you sleep just fine.

## Looking Ahead to Sep 27

Here's where it gets interesting. The Mets head back to Washington for another go-round, and this time we're flipping the script. After missing on the Nationals yesterday, the model's giving us the Mets at 53% with Sean Manaea on the bump against DJ Herz.

I've seen this movie before—when a team drops a winnable game in a series, they tend to come out with a little extra edge the next day. Manaea's been solid down the stretch, and while 53% isn't screaming confidence, it's the kind of slight edge that compounds over a full slate.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Sep 27
content.sub: Pick: Mets 53% | Manaea vs Herz | First pitch from the nation's capital

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

September baseball is all about adjustments. Yesterday the Nationals got us. Tomorrow, we're backing the team that knows what it feels like to lose a game they should've won. The Mets have been battle-tested all season, and Manaea gives them exactly the kind of steady hand you want in this spot.

We're not chasing yesterday's misses—we're following the data where it leads. And right now, it's pointing toward Queens' finest getting back in the win column.

Let's ride.
